judge_assessment.explanation: Every quotient the judge says it recomputed is correct: 168/4=42, 375/5=75, 618/6=103, 2800/7=400, 2835/7=405, 517/4=129 remainder 1, 891/3=297, 858/6=143, 4872/8=609, 3275/6=545 remainder 5, and the judge's cited two-stage ticket item is exact - 4158/7=594 and 594/9=66. The claim that the key 'distinguishes full groups from remainders' is also borne out by problems 10 and 11. But the judge's ACCEPT with instruction_following 4/4 does not survive the prompt's requirement to verify every machine-checkable answer. Problem 6 says 'Write your answer as a quotient with a remainder' and the key boxes '129 R 1', yet verify.json id 6 is a single eval of floor(517/4) with expected 129 - the remainder is never machine-checked, and the Quick Answers bank consequently prints '6. 129', an incomplete answer to the question as asked. A teacher grading from the bank would mark a correct '129 R 1' against a printed '129'.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 10 and 11 pose the identical division (3,275 divided by 6) and change only what the leftover means, and the key states the pedagogy outright: 'problems 10 and 11 are the same division. What changes is what the leftover means ... A student who writes 545 here has answered problem 10 twice.' Keep this paired-item device for remainder interpretation.

Problem 4 estimates 2,835 divided by 7 with the compatible number 2,800 and problem 5 divides it exactly, so the estimate has something concrete to be checked against; the key then uses the estimate to rule out the trap answer 45 'at a glance'.

Seven declared traps (13, 45, 129.1, 69, 546, 545, 594) are each machine-checked as distinguishably wrong and printed in the key's 'Common wrong answers' block, so a wrong paper names its own error; the dropped-zero trap appears at three different place values.

root_causes.description: The verify JSON is authored one entry per problem id rather than one entry per printed response, so a stem that asks for two things is recorded as fully machine verified when only its last component was checked. Nothing in the gate chain compares the number of answer locations the sheet prints against the number of entries covering them.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-112/worksheet.pdf problem 6: 'Divide. Write your answer as a quotient with a remainder.  517 / 4'
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-112/answer_key.pdf problem 6 boxes '129 R 1' and closes 'Check: 4 x 129 + 1 = 516 + 1 = 517'

evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-112/verify.json id 6: {"type": "eval", "expr": "floor(n/4)", "expected": 129} - the only entry for problem 6, with no entry for the remainder 1

improvements.title: Verify every response the worksheet prints a slot for, not only the final numeric result
improvements.proposed_change: Require one verify-JSON entry (machine or manual) per distinct response the sheet asks the student to write, not one per problem id. That covers each lettered sub-part, the remainder half of a 'quotient with a remainder' answer, the person or option a stem asks the learner to name, and every intermediate form a stem explicitly requests before the final one. Enforce it with a gate that counts printed answer locations per problem in the worksheet tex (\ansline, \ansblank, \answerline, and (a)/(b)/(c) part markers inside a \problem stem) and fails the build when a problem's combined machine plus manual entries cover fewer slots than the sheet prints.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture to tests/check_answer_key.py (or the new slot gate) built from curr-112 problem 6: a worksheet stem requesting 'a quotient with a remainder', an answer key boxing '129 R 1', and a verify JSON whose only entry for that id expects 129. The gate must exit non-zero reporting one uncovered response; adding a second entry for 517 - 4*floor(517/4) = 1 must make it exit 0. Today the build reports '12 passed, 0 failed, 0 manual' on exactly this input, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Every printed blank has a checked value behind it, so neither the Quick Answers bank nor a boxed key answer can be a partial answer to the question actually asked.
improvements.risk: Counting slots from tex is heuristic and a stem that prints '(a)' as ordinary prose could raise a false failure. Scope the counter to part markers at the start of a sentence and allow an explicit per-problem slot-count override in the verify JSON.

case_summary: A strong procedural-fluency division packet: all twelve quotients are correct, the long-division cycle is worked place by place in the key with a multiplication check on every item, the ramp runs 1 to 5, and the estimate-then-divide pair and the same-division-two-questions pair are both well constructed. The single real defect is a verification gap: problem 6 explicitly asks for a quotient with a remainder and only the quotient is machine-checked, so the fast-grading bank prints an incomplete answer. Everything else on the sheet has exactly one verify entry per printed response and nothing on it is genuinely open, so the sheet's 'nothing flagged manual' claim is accurate.
